description: Computer engineering students, not vibecoders (except us) and data analysts
summary:
Our project predicts rainfall, humidity, and temperature, schedules potential rainy periods, and recommends the best crops to plant while accounting for climate change. Designed as a free, open-access platform with an intuitive, jargon-free interface, it helps farmers in Mexico—and eventually worldwide—optimize their harvests and decision-making.

The front-end was built in Visual Studio using React, XML, JS, and CSS 5 (with assistance from ChatGPT’s Codex), while data was gathered from NASA POWER via Python alongside precipitation data from Conagua, and deployed on Vercel.
details:
Our project is capable of predicting rainfall, humidity, and temperature; scheduling potential rainy periods; and indicating the best options for planting.

The greatest benefit is that we aim for our application to be free and open-access so that any farmer or agricultural worker can use it, optimizing their harvests and decision-making.

We want our project to make an impact on all Mexican farmers, and we aspire for it to cross borders and help farmers around the world.

The tools we used for front-end development were React, XML, JS, and CSS 5, implemented in the Visual Studio environment, with support from ChatGPT’s Codex for code debugging and executing ideas. The necessary datasets were downloaded from NASA POWER via a terminal using the Python programming language. We used precipitation data from Conagua as a complement to our project. The project was deployed on Vercel.

Our website is innovative because it was designed with the average farmer in mind—someone who may not be familiar with technical or specialized agricultural terminology. We want it to be easy for them to enter parameters and simple to read the results on the page. In other words, we strived to code a user-friendly and intuitive interface for people in the agricultural sector.

We took into account all the factors that affect farmers at the time of planting, as well as the climate change we face today.
